title: Environmentally relevant concentrations of fipronil selectively disrupt venous vessel development in zebrafish embryos/larvae.
authors: Ma, Ya; Zhu, Qicheng; Luo, Shili; Zhang, Fenghong; Liu, Lei; Zhi, Mengxue; Zhang, Zhuyi; Cao, Xiaolian; Qiu, Xuelin; Zeng, Xiangyu; Ji, Di; Li, Chenxin; Zhong, Xiali; Wang, Jianshe; Wei, Yanhong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究农药氟虫腈对斑马鱼胚胎静脉血管发育的选择性毒性，涉及分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作，无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: The pesticide fipronil is widely dispersed in aquatic environments and frequently detected in the general population. Although the adverse effects on embryonic growth by fipronil exposure have been extensively documented, the early responses for its developmental toxicity are largely unknown. In the present study, we explored the sensitive targets of fipronil, focusing on vascular injury using zebrafish embryos/larvae and cultured human endothelial cells. Exposure to 5-500 mug/L fipronil at the early stage impeded the growth of sub-intestinal venous plexus (SIVP), caudal vein plexus (CVP), and common cardinal veins (CCV). The damages on venous vessels occurred at exposure to the environmentally relevant concentration as low as 5 mug/L fipronil, whereas no significant change was observed in general toxicity indexes. In contrast, vascular development of the dorsal aorta (DA) or intersegmental artery (ISA) was not affected. In addition, the mRNA levels of vascular markers and vessel type-specific function genes exhibited significant decreases in venous genes, including nr2f2, ephb4a, and flt4, but no appreciable change in arterial genes. Likewise, the more pronounced changes in cell death and cytoskeleton disruption were shown in human umbilical vein endothelial cells as compared with human aortic endothelial cells. Furthermore, molecular docking supported a stronger affinity of fipronil and its metabolites to the proteins correlated with venous development, such as BMPR2 and SMARCA4. These results reveal the heterogeneity in developing vasculature responsive to fipronil's exposure. The preferential impacts on the veins confer higher sensitivity, allowing them to be appropriate targets for monitoring fipronil's developmental toxicity.
abstract_zh: 杀虫剂氟虫腈在水生环境中广泛分布，并常在普通人群中被检测到。尽管氟虫腈暴露对胚胎生长的不良影响已有大量文献记载，但其发育毒性的早期反应在很大程度上尚不清楚。在本研究中，我们探讨了氟虫腈的敏感靶点，重点关注使用斑马鱼胚胎/幼鱼和培养的人内皮细胞的血管损伤。早期阶段暴露于5-500微克/升的氟虫腈阻碍了肠下静脉丛（SIVP）、尾静脉丛（CVP）和总主静脉（CCV）的生长。静脉血管的损伤发生在暴露于环境相关浓度低至5微克/升氟虫腈时，而一般毒性指标未见显著变化。相反，背主动脉（DA）或节间动脉（ISA）的血管发育未受影响。此外，血管标志物和血管类型特异性功能基因的mRNA水平显示静脉基因显著下降，包括nr2f2、ephb4a和flt4，但动脉基因无明显变化。同样，与人主动脉内皮细胞相比，人脐静脉内皮细胞在细胞死亡和细胞骨架破坏方面表现出更显著的变化。此外，分子对接支持氟虫腈及其代谢物与静脉发育相关蛋白（如BMPR2和SMARCA4）具有更强的亲和力。这些结果揭示了发育中血管系统对氟虫腈暴露反应的异质性。对静脉的优先影响赋予了更高的敏感性，使其成为监测氟虫腈发育毒性的合适靶点。
